how_point_ended.question: How did this tennis point end?
options: Ace: is when the server scores in the first shot. The receiver didn’t touch the ball.
Double Fault: The server misses both first and second serves, resulting in an automatic point for the opponent.
Winner: When a shot (other than serve) lands in and isn’t touched or can’t be returned. Clean shot not returned (excluding net winners)

Forced Error: error caused due to pressure from the opponent’s aggressive or well-placed shot. e.g., rushed forehand sent long after a powerful serve or wide angle. The opponent pressured into an error.

Unforced Error: player makes a mistake during the point without significant pressure such as hitting the ball outside of the court (long or wide) or into the net during a routine shot. Routine miss without pressure.
Violation: Rule-based loss of point includes player touching net, ball touches player, double bounce, foot fault, etc.
Retirement/Default: Player stops playing due to injury or penalty
Let: "Point Replayed", point doesn't end. For example when the ball clips the net on serve and lands in (replay the serve) or when there is external disturbance (crowd noise, ball on court)

mcq_how_point_ended_description_mechanis.question: Describe in detail how this point ended between <player1> and <player2>. (<player1> - <player1_description>, <player2> - <player2_description>)
mcq_how_point_ended_description_mechanis.llm_question_prompt: Generate 3 plausible but incorrect descriptions by changing ONLY the mechanism of how the point ends while keeping the winner and player roles unchanged. Prioritize common confusions: net-cord dribbler winner vs into the net error, ball IN vs OUT calls ('clips/lands on the line' [in] vs 'out of bounds'), ace vs regular rally, double fault vs rally error, and serve let (point replay) vs point-ending rally or ace. Do NOT change which player wins or who commits the error; do NOT change location descriptors (left/right/center, doubles alley vs baseline/sideline); do NOT add unsupported details (serve count, stroke type, rally length, score). Maintain the original simple, direct sentence structure and use precise tennis terms ('net cord', 'into the net', 'on the line', 'in', 'out of bounds', 'past the baseline', 'beyond the singles sideline'). Avoid generic options such as 'unforced error', 'net violation', 'defensive lob', 'lucky shot'. Keep each option concise (<= 120 characters).
